title: Where does rain come from?
examples: How does water get up into the sky?
What happens when the rain falls back down?

explain.say: Look up high in the sky. You can see big white clouds floating there.

draw.text: Clouds are made of tiny water droplets.

explain.say: Now look! Here it is in 3D: the water cycle. Can you see the sun and the evaporation? Tap any part, and I will tell you about it.
The little droplets in the clouds bump into each other. They join together to get bigger.

draw.text: Droplets join to form bigger clouds.

explain.say: When the clouds get too heavy, they cannot hold all the water anymore.
The water falls down from the sky as rain. This is how we get water to drink.

draw.text: Rain falls from the sky to Earth.

explain.say: When the rain hits the ground, it goes into rivers and underground. Then the sun helps it go up again.
If you see a puddle on the ground, the sun heats it up. The water goes up as invisible gas.

draw.text: Sun heats puddles, water goes up.

faq.a: No, clouds can also make snow or hail. They are just carrying water in different forms.
asks: Can clouds make other things besides rain?
What else can come out of a cloud?

faq.q: Why is the water invisible when it goes up?
faq.a: When water gets very warm, it turns into a gas called water vapor. You cannot see this gas.
asks: Why does the water disappear into the sky?

faq.q: Does the rain always fall straight down?
faq.a: Sometimes the wind blows the rain sideways. It can also drizzle gently for a long time.

faq.q: How long does this water cycle take?
faq.a: The water cycle never stops. It happens all the time, every day, all over the world.
asks: Is the water cycle fast or slow?
Does the water cycle ever end?

faq.q: What is the difference between rain and mist?
faq.a: Rain falls from clouds in drops. Mist is just very small water droplets floating near the ground.
asks: What is the difference between fog and rain?

facts: Water evaporates from rivers and oceans.
Clouds form when water vapor cools and turns back into liquid.
Precipitation is the water falling back to Earth.
The water cycle keeps Earth's water fresh.

quiz.say: Water turns into gas when heated by the sun. This process is called:
quiz.why: Evaporation is the scientific word for liquid turning into gas.

wrong.0: Condensation is when gas turns back into liquid, like in clouds.
wrong.1: Precipitation is the water falling from the sky.
wrong.2: Collection just means the water gathering in one place.

quiz.say: When water vapor cools down high in the sky, it forms:
quiz.why: Cooling gas makes tiny droplets that group together to make clouds.

wrong.1: Rivers are water that has already fallen to the ground.
wrong.2: Vapor is the gas form that is floating up.
wrong.3: The sun provides the heat for the whole cycle.

quiz.say: If you see water droplets joining together in the sky, what stage of the cycle are you seeing?
quiz.why: Joining droplets is the key part of condensation, making the cloud.

wrong.0: Collection is the water gathered on the ground.
wrong.2: Evaporation is the start, when water goes up as gas.
wrong.3: Rainfall is the end, when the water comes down.
